summary.intent: Determine whether Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability/correctness) needed a discuss step before planning, reconcile stale/pending todos against Phases 70-71, then run the full GSD plan→execute→ship flow for Phase 72 (with Phase 73 to follow) — work that was interrupted by two production CI regressions and a web-e2e flakiness investigation which had to be resolved first.
summary.outcome: Both CI regressions (FUSE seq-1 equivocation in desktop-e2e via PR #601, and a stale IndexedDB floor-store test helper plus sdk-e2e Test 21 idempotency assertion via PR #600) were root-caused, fixed, validated via local/dispatched CI runs, and merged to main. Web-e2e flakiness across 4 tests was diagnosed and fixed at source (no retries added). Phase 72 was then planned (10 plans/7 waves, research + pattern-mapping + plan-checker all passed) and executed through Wave 6 of 7, with 9/10 plans landed cleanly (SC#1 delete/resurrection guard, SC#2 fail-closed, SC#3 restore re-homing, SC#4 listingCache invalidation, SC#5 dead-branch removal, SC#6 write-key-walk + TEE-wrap dedup all green); a new todo was filed to fix vitest v2→v3 Mock-type drift in test files and wire test-inclusive typecheck into CI as a follow-up plan (72-11) before ship.

repo: `ci-e2e.yml` (Web/Desktop E2E) only triggers on push-to-main or `workflow_dispatch`, never on PRs — dispatch via `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (the `-f ref=` form 422s if main's workflow definition predates that input)

Playwright web-e2e `ciFloor()` helper only raises wait timeouts (30s→60s) under `CI=1`; locally these waits are tight and cause flaky cascades on IPNS-gated ops even when CI would pass — running with `CI=1` locally requires patching `webServer.reuseExistingServer` (hardcoded `!process.env.CI`) to avoid refusing to reuse an already-running dev stack

`pnpm typecheck` in CI only runs each package's `build` (tsconfig.build.json, tests excluded) plus tsconfig.scripts.json — test files are never typechecked in CI, even though the base tsconfig.json includes them, so vitest-v2→v3 Mock-generic drift accumulates silently in test files without failing CI
Fresh git worktrees in this pnpm monorepo lack `node_modules` — a known failure mode for GSD's worktree-based parallel wave execution; sequential execution on the main tree sidesteps it
Local API dist can go stale mid-session and start rejecting `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`; restarting the API from source fixes it (recurring known pattern)

Phase 71 (#599) shipped with three separate pieces of test/fixture drift left unfixed: stale share DTO field names in `.mts` desktop-e2e driver (`readDescriptorRef`→`encryptedReadKey`, `rootIpnsName`→`shareRootIpnsName`), a self-inconsistent sdk-e2e Test 21 idempotency assertion, and an unaddressed FUSE seq-1 equivocation bug

`git status`/`cat-file` checks against HEAD can appear to disagree with what's actually committed during multi-commit planner runs — decisive verification requires re-checking HEAD tree contents directly rather than trusting a first read

code.finding: `publish_file_node`'s first-publish branch hardcoded seq=1 gated only by 'inode cid empty'; a dropped/stale UploadComplete retry re-triggers it with a fresh CID at seq=1, tripping Phase 71's anti-equivocation gate. Fixed by resolving IPNS first via `resolve_ipns_for_replay`: NotFound→genuine first-publish, Found(seq)→route into `publish_with_cas_retry` with the resolved seq (not skip, since content differs from replay.rs's skip-on-Found case).

`publish_with_cas_retry` extended with optional `preresolved_seq: Option<u64>` to avoid a redundant second IPNS resolve on the just-resolved `Found` path (Greptile P2 perf nit); conflict-retry path always re-resolves since a pre-resolved value is stale after conflict.

Text editor re-resolves file content fresh from the live API on every open (downloadFromIpns→resolveIpnsRecord→resolveFileMetadata→downloadFileContent, none cached) — explains why a naive post-restore version-count check race-reads stale content.

The 6.6.2 restore test's `getVersionCount()===1` gate is a no-op since restore swaps current↔v1 leaving the past-version count at 1 both before and after — provided zero synchronization wait for the restore's IPNS republish, causing a race read of stale editor content.

workflow: When a background subagent/CI monitor delivers a result, verify the actual failing test signature before trusting a hypothesis (e.g. re-checking whether the same spec failed twice vs a different spec each run) to distinguish deterministic regressions from suite flakiness

For unattended overnight/AFK execution, capture directives that surface mid-flight (e.g. 'fix all TS drift + wire CI typecheck') as a durable todo file immediately, then sequence them as a final phase plan rather than deferring silently — keeps autonomous execution auditable

Use `expect.poll()` over a single assertion read when validating async state after a mutation that has no explicit completion signal, rather than a proxy condition that can be trivially true both before and after (as with the version-count no-op gate)

Rebase a long-lived PR branch onto main before dispatching a full validation CI run when a sibling PR merged mid-flight and touches shared runtime code (e.g. #601's FUSE fix), so the dispatched run reflects true post-merge state rather than failing on stale code

GSD `plan:pre` hook fragments are stored as JSON with literal (non-escaped) control characters in string values, breaking both `jq`/direct JSON.parse and naive regex extraction — required writing a lenient parser script to escape control chars only inside string literals

friction: Repeated local Playwright runs cascaded on a different early flaky test each time (4.10 batch delete → 4.11 batch move → 2.1 create-folder) due to tight local timeouts vs CI's 60s `ciFloor`, blocking verification of the actual target fixes (6.6.2/8.2) across 5 separate reruns before switching to a CI-equivalent `CI=1` regime
`gh workflow run -f ref=` returned HTTP 422 because the target workflow definition predated the `ref` input — required discovering `--ref <branch>` as the workaround
`git commit` via lint-staged hung/timed out (~2m), apparently on a 1Password SSH signing prompt — required a follow-up check to confirm the commit actually landed before retrying
Initially checked the wrong todo directory (`resolved/` instead of `completed/`), corrected by the user mid-turn
`cargo check`/rustfmt for winfsp fails locally on macOS due to `windows-future` not compiling — a known cross-platform limitation requiring Windows CI as the authoritative check
GSD hook JSON extraction failed via direct jq/regex due to unescaped control characters, requiring a custom Node script to parse it

AskUserQuestion was answered with a meta-question ('is there anything to discuss?') rather than a direct choice, requiring the assistant to actually read all 9 todos to answer definitively before re-asking
